items.stem: What is the best way to make sure an audience can follow your talk?

options.text: Organise it around a few clear points in order
options.rationale: Correct: clear structure helps the audience follow.

options.text: Say as many facts as fast as you can
Read silently so nobody is disturbed
options.rationale: A talk must be spoken to be heard.

options.text: Turn your back to the audience
options.rationale: Facing away makes you hard to hear and see.

items.explanation: Correct: clear structure helps the audience follow.

items.stem: Why are pauses useful when speaking?

options.text: They give the audience time to take in your point
options.rationale: Correct: pauses aid understanding and emphasis.

options.text: They prove you have forgotten everything
options.rationale: A planned pause is a tool, not a mistake.

options.text: They make the talk sound like a robot
options.rationale: Natural pauses sound human, not robotic.

options.text: They are only for the ending
options.rationale: Pauses can be used throughout a talk.

items.explanation: Correct: pauses aid understanding and emphasis.

items.stem: Which TWO habits help you connect with your audience? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Making eye contact with different people
Speaking clearly and loudly enough to be heard
options.rationale: Correct: clear, audible speech reaches the audience.
Mumbling makes you hard to understand.

options.text: Hiding behind a desk the whole time
